samples.summary: New window-level Esc handler navigates away when Esc is used to dismiss the ShareDialog on the same page
samples.evidence: `ImageFileLayout` renders `<ShareDialog documentId={documentId} />` (packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-detail.tsx:148) inside the same subtree as `<ImageViewer onClose={close}>`. ShareDialog is a Radix `Dialog` (packages/frontend/src/components/share-dialog.tsx:155-171) with no `onEscapeKeyDown` override and no `stopPropagation`, so an Esc that dismisses the dialog also reaches the new `window` keydown listener in image-viewer.tsx:126. The dialog's focused element is `DialogContent` (a div), so the INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable guard at image-viewer.tsx:116-123 does not suppress it — the user closes the share dialog and is simultaneously navigated out of the viewer to the documents list. Fix belongs on the new handler (ignore Esc when an overlay/dismissable layer is open, or scope the listener to the viewer container).

samples.summary: Esc that closes the mobile sidebar Sheet will also trigger the viewer's new navigate-away
samples.evidence: `FileShell` mounts `AppSidebar` inside `SidebarProvider`; on mobile the sidebar renders as a Radix `Sheet` (Dialog) at packages/frontend/src/components/ui/sidebar.tsx:184-203. Pressing Esc to dismiss that sheet bubbles to the new window-level Esc handler (packages/frontend/src/app/files/image-viewer.tsx:126), whose target is a div and so passes the input guard — the sheet closes and the route changes in one keystroke. Same for the header's NotificationBell Popover (packages/frontend/src/components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx:46-64), which is rendered in every SiteHeader. Fix belongs on the new Esc handler.

samples.summary: Back button / Esc can navigate to /documents while the workspaces query is still in flight
samples.evidence: `useDocumentsPath` defaults `workspaces` to `[]` while the `["workspaces"]` query loads, so it returns "/documents" until data arrives (packages/frontend/src/app/files/use-documents-path.ts:17-21). The new back button (file-detail.tsx:139) and Esc handler are reachable immediately on mount — a fast Esc lands on the workspace-less list instead of the documented `/w/:slug` destination. Previously only FileShell's error redirect had this race; the change extends it to a user-triggered control. Gating on `isPending`/`isSuccess` would remove it.

verdict.reason: All elements of the claim check out in the repo. image-viewer.tsx:113-130 installs a bubble-phase window keydown listener that calls onClose() on Escape with no defaultPrevented check; its only suppression is an INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable target test (lines 116-123). file-detail.tsx:148 renders <ShareDialog> in the same mounted subtree as <ImageViewer onClose={close}> (file-detail.tsx:152), where close navigates away (file-detail.tsx:131-134). share-dialog.tsx:155-171 passes no onEscapeKeyDown/onKeyDown/stopPropagation, and the shadcn wrapper ui/dialog.tsx:47-71 merely forwards props to DialogPrimitive.Content, adding no Esc interception. Radix's dismissable layer calls preventDefault(), not stopPropagation(), so the Esc that dismisses the dialog also bubbles to the window listener; focus is on DialogContent or a BUTTON/SelectTrigger, so the INPUT/TEXTAREA guard does not apply. file-shell.tsx:108-131, the common wrapper, adds no key handling either — no guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. This is in the blast-radius lane (a new global listener changing behaviour for an existing, untouched consumer on the same page) and major by impact: one Esc both closes the share dialog and navigates the user out of the viewer.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. image-viewer.tsx:113-130 registers a window-level keydown listener whose only guard is target tagName INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable; it does not check e.defaultPrevented or whether an overlay is open, and calls onClose() (a navigate) on Escape at line 126. sidebar.tsx:182-205 does render the mobile sidebar as a Radix Sheet/Dialog, and notification-bell.tsx:46-65 renders a Radix Popover that site-header.tsx:99 mounts in every header. Radix's DismissableLayer dismisses on Escape from a document-level capture listener that calls preventDefault but not stopPropagation, so the same keystroke still reaches the window bubble listener; focus inside those overlays is on a div/button, which passes the input-only guard. The viewer with onClose is genuinely inside that shell: file-detail.tsx:152 mounts ImageViewer with onClose inside FileShell, and file-shell.tsx:109-125 wraps it in SidebarProvider/AppSidebar/SiteHeader (ShareDialog at file-detail.tsx:148 is affected the same way). Existing tests (image-viewer.test.tsx:52-60) only cover the INPUT case, so no guard makes this unreachable. This is a new behaviour whose out-of-diff consumers (overlay components) were not considered — in-lane and blocking at major.
